## Scope and identities

The suite retains all 28 variants, 56 declared trials and original per-trial turn/time/repetition caps; the other 27 variants are unchanged. The independent_malicious scorer is unchanged. ## Smallest verification bridge

Root's proposed two-file test bridge is sufficient for this fixture migration increment: test setup must read captured context-binding.json.source_write_paths as a required well-typed array when a declaration exists, with legacy scope.write_paths only when the declaration is absent. The reusable source-preparation tool should preserve exact declared limits and unresolved profile, copy only into an owned absent local destination, bind the actual generated base/head and full fixture/suite digests, and retain provenance. # Native source preparation tool v1 review

Two concrete bounded-capture/output-namespace concerns and one documentation mismatch were reported. No tool, test, Git, Cargo, fixture program, native process or provider operation was executed. All three held draft hashes match FILES e30432a90778331834ebf3f577093359aee061eafcf9331504babbff7a6584d6; patch 4cfdf40f26cf581e49029e2dd7f0ea978bb5c50c0ced20654f2897a64249c1f3. Original artifact remains unchanged.

1. `capture.walk` materializes `sorted(os.listdir(fd))` before checking MAX_ENTRIES. Oversized supplied directories allocate their complete names list before the 4096-entry refusal, including on the final checking pass. Use bounded descriptor-backed iteration, then sort only the bounded list, and enforce a limit on every pass.

2. The output parent is checked for canonical spelling and current UID, but not for group/world write access. Path-based output/child creation, materialization and Git cwd follow after the one-time check. Another writer of that parent can rename the newly created output and substitute a directory/symlink, redirecting child creation before a later capture detects it. At minimum require a protected current-user-owned parent and retain/recheck output inode around path-based phases; descriptor-relative exclusive creation and retained root identities provide a stronger invariant.
